title: Summarize weekly business metrics into a one-page report
summary: Paste this week's and last week's numbers and get a short one-page report with changes, a plain summary, and a few next actions. You check the math before sharing.

tests.prompt:
Create a one-page weekly business report from these numbers.

Week ending: [DATE]
This week metrics (paste as labeled lines): [SALES / REVENUE], [PIPELINE OR NEW LEADS], [MARKETING — e.g. spend, clicks, signups], [EXPENSES OR CASH], [OTHER KPIs YOU TRACK]
Last week metrics (same labels): [PASTE]
Notes I already know (optional): [CONTEXT — launches, outages, seasonality]

Output:
Title: Weekly business performance — [DATE]
For each metric section: this week, last week, % change (say "n/a" if last week missing)
Overall summary: 2–3 sentences in plain words
Watch-outs: up to 3 bullets (only if supported by the numbers)
Do-next: up to 3 concrete actions

Rules: Do not invent metrics. Do not claim causes you were not given. Keep the whole report skimmable in under two minutes.

setup.agent: Chat model each week; optional Make/Zapier to assemble exports into one prompt
steps: Export key numbers from CRM, ads, and accounting into one paste block.
Include last week's numbers in the same shape.
Run the prompt and skim every percentage.
Edit the summary, then save as a doc or PDF for your team.
Optional: schedule a Friday automation that emails you the filled prompt.
setup.approvalStep: Verify totals and % changes before anyone else sees the report.
failureModes: Wrong percent change from mismatched units
Burying the one number that actually matters

toolPicks.why: Pull multiple exports into one weekly prompt.
toolPicks.whenNot: All numbers already live in one sheet.
You prefer a manual Friday ritual.

toolPicks.why: Sales and pipeline figures in one export.
toolPicks.whenNot: Sales is not part of this report.

faq.q: How often should I run this?
faq.a: Weekly is a solid default. Switch to monthly if the numbers barely move.

faq.q: What if formats differ across tools?
faq.a: Normalize labels before pasting, or tell the model what each column means. Do not trust mixed units.
